# CORE

> A project-intelligence agent for Claude Code (and Codex). It knows your whole project across sessions, surfaces decisions and risks before you ask, and challenges overconfidence. You install it as a plugin and drive it with the `/core` slash command.

CORE is a single agent backed by a unit-based memory store (one fact per file, with typed links), a four-tier retrieval ladder, and a rendered six-section project synthesis (`PROJECT.md`). It reaches for multi-agent adversarial review only when the stakes warrant it — that's one tool, not the product. It runs on Claude Code today and is built to be harness-agnostic.

## Start here

- [README.md](README.md): what CORE is, why it exists, how it works, and install commands.
- [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md): install on Claude Code or Codex, run a local copy, troubleshoot.
- [USAGE.md](USAGE.md): the reference for every command (`/core`, eight companions, and one deprecation shim), every protocol, and the scripts you would run or read directly.

## How to use it

- **Install (Claude Code):** `/plugin marketplace add dbatesai/core-plugin` then `/plugin install core@core`. From the terminal: `claude plugins marketplace add dbatesai/core-plugin` then `claude plugins install core@core`.
- **Run:** type `/core` to start or resume a project. It loads your project context and prints a readiness summary before doing anything else.
- **Companions:** `/finalize` (close a session), `/refocus` (recenter mid-session on what matters most now, given what you've learned since you started), `/process-memory` (memory housekeeping on demand), `/register-sources` (point CORE at an outside data source), `/configure-project` (bootstrap and health-check a project), `/vibecheck` (capture the session's vibe), `/metrics` (the one door to memory health — plain-language answers by default, with `full`/`export`/`self-test` modes), `/memory-view` (browse the memory store as a read-only page, published as a private artifact only after an explicit, per-publish confirmation). - **Deprecation shim:** `/orient` folded into `/core`; it still registers and forwards (removal scheduled 2026-08-15).
